subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which prominent opposition leader and social reformer presided over the founding congress of the Socialist Party in Patna in 1949?
questions.explanation: Acharya Narendra Deva was a founding stalwart of Indian democratic socialism and guided the Socialist Party after it severed ties with Congress in 1948.

questions.question: Which princely state was ruled by a Hindu Maharaja named Hari Singh while having a predominantly Muslim population in 1947?
questions.explanation: Jammu and Kashmir was ruled by Maharaja Hari Singh, who initially hoped to preserve independence before Pakistani tribal aggression compelled him to accede to India.

questions.question: The famous slogan 'Languages are many, but India is one' was tested when which southern state was rocked by intense anti-Hindi language agitations in January 1965?
questions.explanation: Widespread violent agitations broke out in Madras State in January 1965 when Hindi was slated to become the sole official language of the Union under Article 343.

questions.question: In which state of India was the landmark Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) multipurpose river project constructed during the First Five Year Plan?
options: D) West Bengal and Bihar (now Jharkhand)
questions.explanation: The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was established in July 1948 modeled on the US Tennessee Valley Authority, operating across West Bengal and Bihar.

questions.question: Which of the following states was the primary beneficiary and epicenter of the early Green Revolution in wheat production?
questions.explanation: Punjab, with its extensive canal irrigation and fertile soils, was the vanguard state that achieved spectacular yield gains during the early Green Revolution.

questions.question: Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution enjoins the state to 'promote international peace and security'?
questions.explanation: Article 51 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to promote international peace and security, maintain just relations between nations, and foster respect for international law.

questions.question: Which country provided critical diplomatic veto support in the UN Security Council to India during the 1971 Bangladesh crisis?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union cast three consecutive vetoes in the UN Security Council in December 1971, blocking US-backed ceasefire resolutions aimed at halting Indian operations in East Pakistan.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who served as the Prime Minister of India following Lal Bahadur Shastri's sudden demise in Tashkent in January 1966?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi defeated Morarji Desai in a secret ballot of Congress MPs in January 1966 to become India's third Prime Minister.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The fourth General Election held in February 1967 was famously described by contemporary political commentators as a:
questions.explanation: Political analysts characterized the 1967 election results as a 'political earthquake' because Congress lost power in eight major states and suffered sharp declines in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: What preventive detention legislation was aggressively used during the Emergency of 1975-1977 to incarcerate opposition politicians without trial?
options: A) Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Act (TADA)
B) Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA)
D) Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA)
questions.explanation: MISA was used to detain tens of thousands of political leaders, journalists, and activists without judicial trial during the Emergency.

questions.question: Which political party was formed in early 1977 by combining Congress(O), Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Bharatiya Lok Dal, and the Socialist Party to defeat Indira Gandhi?
questions.explanation: The Janata Party was formed on the eve of the March 1977 elections, uniting major non-communist opposition groups under the inspiration of Jayaprakash Narayan.

questions.question: Which hill state in the Northeast was granted statehood in 1972 through the carving out of autonomous hill districts from Assam?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya was created as an autonomous state within Assam in 1970 and elevated to full statehood on 21 January 1972.

questions.question: Which charismatic leader founded the Dravida Kazhagam (DK) in 1944, leading the social justice movement in southern India?
questions.explanation: Periyar transformed the Justice Party into Dravida Kazhagam (DK) in 1944, campaigning against caste discrimination, Brahminical orthodoxy, and northern dominance.

questions.question: Who served as the Deputy Prime Minister in the National Front government formed under Prime Minister V.P. Singh in 1989?
questions.explanation: Choudhary Devi Lal, a powerful peasant leader from Haryana, served as Deputy Prime Minister in V.P. Singh's National Front government.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In which month and year did Mikhail Gorbachev formally resign as President of the Soviet Union, handing nuclear codes to Boris Yeltsin?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991, and the Soviet red hammer-and-sickle flag atop the Kremlin was replaced with the Russian tricolor.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following was the direct collective defense military alliance of Western capitalist nations formed in April 1949?
questions.explanation: NATO was founded on 4 April 1949 by 12 Western nations led by the United States to provide collective security against Soviet aggression.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: The currency known as the 'Euro' serves as the official monetary unit for member states of which supranational union?
questions.explanation: The Euro is the official currency of the Eurozone, currently shared by 20 of the European Union's 27 member states.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following countries is an island state in East Asia that achieved rapid post-war industrial reconstruction guided by a pacifist constitution?
questions.explanation: Japan rebuilt its economy after World War II to become the second-largest economy in the world by the late 20th century under its pacifist 1947 constitution.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which country separated from Pakistan in December 1971 following a nine-month war of national liberation?
questions.explanation: East Pakistan seceded and became the sovereign nation of Bangladesh in December 1971 following the Pakistani military crackdown and Indian intervention.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which island country was the presidential system replaced by a competitive multi-party parliamentary democracy in 2005?
questions.explanation: In June 2005, the Parliament of Maldives voted unanimously to introduce a multi-party democratic political system.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: How many sovereign member states are currently represented in the United Nations General Assembly?
questions.explanation: The United Nations General Assembly has 193 sovereign member states, with South Sudan admitted as the 193rd member in 2011.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which principal judicial organ of the United Nations is tasked with settling legal disputes submitted to it by states?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice, based at The Hague, is the principal judicial organ of the UN.

questions.question: What is the traditional alliance-building practice where weaker nations align with a stronger hegemon rather than opposing it termed in security studies?
questions.explanation: Bandwagoning occurs when a state chooses to ally with a dominant power to share the benefits of its strength rather than balance against it.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which 1987 United Nations report first popularized the definition of 'Sustainable Development' as meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs?
options: D) The Brundtland Report (Our Common Future)
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Commission's report 'Our Common Future' (1987) provided the universally accepted definition of sustainable development.

questions.question: In which city did delegates from worldwide social movements gather in January 2004 for the fourth World Social Forum (WSF) meeting, held in India?
questions.explanation: The 2004 World Social Forum met in Mumbai, India, bringing together over 100,000 activists from labor unions, peasant federations, and environmental groups.

questions.question: Which leader was appointed as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and later served as free India's first Law Minister?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and steered the enactment of the Indian Constitution, joining Nehru's first cabinet as Law Minister.

questions.question: What was the significance of the States Reorganisation Act enacted by Parliament in August 1956?
options: A) It abolished all regional languages in favor of Sanskrit and English
B) It merged all princely state territories into five administrative zones
C) It redrew state boundaries primarily on linguistic lines, creating 14 States and 6 Union Territories
D) It banned the formation of political parties based on linguistic representation
questions.explanation: Enacted pursuant to the Fazal Ali Commission report, the 1956 Act restructured the Indian map into 14 linguistic states and 6 union territories.

questions.question: Why did critics like J.C. Kumarappa criticize the heavy industrial emphasis of the Second Five Year Plan?
options: A) Because it banned the construction of hydroelectric dams and canal irrigation
B) Because it relied exclusively on private American multinational banks for financing
C) Because it prohibited the cultivation of food crops in northern Indian states
D) Because it neglected decentralized village industries, generated urban unemployment, and drained resources away from rural artisans
questions.explanation: Gandhian economist J.C. Kumarappa argued that large-scale centralized industrialization displaced rural labor and advocated self-reliant village-centered agro-industries.

questions.question: What was the immediate cause of the armed conflict between India and Pakistan in September 1965?
options: A) Pakistan's covert infiltration of armed personnel into Jammu and Kashmir under 'Operation Gibraltar' to instigate a local rebellion
B) A disputed maritime naval clash near the port of Karachi
C) An aerial bombing raid on New Delhi by the Pakistani air force
D) The unilateral construction of a mega-dam across the Jhelum river by India
questions.explanation: In August 1965, Pakistan launched Operation Gibraltar, sending thousands of covert infiltrators across the ceasefire line in Kashmir, escalating into full-scale war.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which of the following was a key component of Indira Gandhi's radical 'Ten-Point Programme' adopted in May 1967?
options: A) Abolition of all progressive income taxation for corporate enterprises
B) Social control of banks, nationalisation of general insurance, and ceilings on urban property and income
C) Immediate privatization of all state-owned railways and coal mines
D) Compulsory military training for all university graduates
questions.explanation: The Ten-Point Programme embraced socialist policies including social control of banking institutions, nationalisation of insurance, public food distribution, and curbs on monopolies.

questions.question: What major socio-political change did the student movement in Gujarat in 1974 successfully achieve under the leadership of the Navnirman Yuvak Samiti?
options: A) It forced India to withdraw from the Non-Aligned Movement
B) It resulted in the partition of Gujarat into two unilingual states
C) It forced the resignation of Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel and the dissolution of the Gujarat State Legislative Assembly
D) It led to the immediate privatization of all state universities in western India
questions.explanation: Intense student agitation and Morarji Desai's indefinite fast forced the central government to dissolve the Gujarat Assembly in March 1974.

questions.question: What did the Shah Commission conclude regarding the arrests of political leaders made on the night of 25 June 1975 before the formal proclamation of Emergency?
options: A) That the arrests were fully sanctioned by individual High Court judicial warrants
B) That the detainees were foreign armed spies infiltrating across the border
C) That the arrests were ordered unanimously by a special session of Parliament
D) That the arrests were completely illegal and carried out on verbal orders before the proclamation was signed by the President
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission found that dozens of opposition leaders were rounded up on verbal instructions hours before the President signed the Emergency proclamation.

questions.question: What was the central grievance articulated by the All Assam Students Union (AASU) during its movement from 1979 to 1985?
options: A) That large-scale undocumented migration from Bangladesh was threatening the cultural identity and political rights of indigenous Assamese people
B) That Assam should secede from the Indian Union and join the United Nations
C) That oil refineries in Assam should be dismantled and shifted to central India
D) That the tea plantations of Assam should be handed over to foreign corporations
questions.explanation: AASU campaigned against the presence of millions of undocumented foreigners on Assam's electoral rolls, demanding their detection, disenfranchisement, and deportation.

questions.question: Why did the minority United Front government of 1996 choose H.D. Deve Gowda as its consensus Prime Minister?
options: A) Because he held an absolute personal majority in the Rajya Sabha
B) Because he was an acceptable regional leader from southern India belonging to the Janata Dal who was not associated with bitter north Indian factional disputes
C) Because he was nominated directly by the President without parliamentary consultation
D) Because the Communist Party insisted on appointing a member of the armed forces
questions.explanation: When Jyoti Basu was barred by the CPI(M) Politburo from accepting the prime ministership, Karnataka Chief Minister H.D. Deve Gowda emerged as the consensus candidate.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'consensus' that has emerged across major political parties in India since the 1990s despite coalition competition?
options: A) Consensus on abolishing the multi-party democratic system in favor of one-party rule
B) Consensus on withdrawing India from the United Nations and the World Trade Organization
C) Broad consensus on new economic policies (liberalisation), acceptance of OBC reservation, and the increasing role of regional parties in governance
D) Consensus on nationalising all private agricultural land and manufacturing units
questions.explanation: Despite ideological contestation, Indian parties reached a four-fold consensus: support for economic reforms, acceptance of backward-caste reservations, acceptance of coalition governance, and pragmatism over ideology.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What was the main reason why economic reforms in China succeeded rapidly while 'Shock Therapy' caused catastrophic collapse in Russia?
options: A) China borrowed all of its investment capital from Soviet state banks
B) Russia possessed no natural gas, petroleum, or mineral resources
C) China completely banned all foreign trade and investment from the West
D) China followed a gradual, state-guided transition starting with agriculture and SEZs, whereas Russia attempted sudden overnight privatisation of state assets
questions.explanation: China phased its reforms step-by-step under firm political control (agriculture in 1982, industry in 1998), while post-Soviet Russia unleashed abrupt price deregulation and privatisation.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary function of the European Commission, headquartered in Brussels, Belgium?
options: A) Acting as the executive branch of the EU, proposing new European legislation, and managing EU policies and the budget
B) Operating as the supreme military high command for NATO across Western Europe
C) Conducting criminal investigations into national murder cases in member states
D) Directly setting the interest rates for commercial retail banks in London and Paris
questions.explanation: The European Commission is the politically independent executive arm of the EU, alone responsible for drawing up proposals for new European legislation.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What was the primary goal of the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement signed by SAARC countries in 2004?
options: A) Creating a single common currency (the South Asian Rupee) across all member nations
B) Lowering customs tariffs and eliminating trade barriers to create a free trade zone across South Asian nations
C) Forming a collective military defense pact against Southeast Asian states
D) Banning all imports of electronic goods manufactured in East Asia
questions.explanation: SAFTA was signed in January 2004 in Islamabad to reduce customs duties on traded goods among SAARC nations, entering into effect on 1 January 2006.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which independent international human rights organisation based in London was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977 for its campaign against torture and defense of political prisoners?
questions.explanation: Amnesty International, founded in 1961 by Peter Benenson, won the 1977 Nobel Peace Prize for defending prisoners of conscience and campaigning against torture.

questions.question: What is the distinction between 'Traditional External Security' and 'Traditional Internal Security'?
options: A) External security handles trade tariffs, while internal security handles income tax collection
B) External security protects private corporations, while internal security protects public universities
C) External security applies only to naval forces, while internal security applies exclusively to air forces
D) External security deals with military threats to sovereignty and territory from foreign states, while internal security deals with maintaining law, order, and peace within the nation's borders
questions.explanation: Traditional security addresses external threats (military invasion by another state) and internal threats (civil war, separatist violence, breakdown of domestic law and order).

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which of the following areas is recognized as part of the 'Global Commons' under international environmental agreements?
options: A) Outer space, the high seas, the deep ocean floor, and the Antarctic continent
B) All national agricultural farmland across North America
C) The territorial river basins of the Rhine, Danube, and Ganges
D) Private oil refineries located along the coast of the Persian Gulf
questions.explanation: Global commons are resource domains that do not fall within the sovereign jurisdiction of any single nation: the atmosphere, outer space, the oceans, and Antarctica.

questions.question: How do right-wing political critics in developing countries view the political consequences of economic globalisation?
options: A) They argue that globalization forces all countries to adopt Soviet-style collective farming
B) They fear that globalization weakens the sovereign authority and autonomy of the national state in making independent decisions
C) They believe that globalization will eliminate all private corporate businesses
D) They assert that globalization will double the size of the national civil service bureaucracy
questions.explanation: Political critics from the right argue that sovereign state authority is eroded by international treaties, multinational corporations, and global capital flows.

questions.question: Which political thinker formulated the concept of 'Saptakranti' (Seven Revolutions) to achieve total democratic socialist transformation in India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia propounded 'Saptakranti'—seven revolutions targeting gender inequality, caste hierarchy, colonial racism, economic inequality, armed weapons, and state tyranny.

questions.question: Under which constitutional draft provision did the Government of India introduce the 'Sixth Schedule' to protect tribal autonomy and customary laws in the northeastern hill regions?
options: A) Complete abolition of all traditional tribal village councils across the northeast
B) Mandatory replacement of tribal customary laws with central civil penal codes
C) Appointment of military governors with absolute veto power over tribal affairs
D) Creation of Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) with legislative and judicial powers
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule, based on the Bordoloi Sub-Committee report, established Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram to safeguard tribal autonomy.

questions.question: In which landmark Supreme Court ruling did a 5-judge Constitution Bench strike down the First Amendment's provisions on land reform before the 9th Schedule was affirmed?
options: A) Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar (1951)
B) Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
C) Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
questions.explanation: When the Patna High Court struck down the Bihar Land Reforms Act in Kameshwar Singh (1951), Parliament enacted the First Amendment, creating the Ninth Schedule to immunize land reform laws.

questions.question: Which secret strategic military operation was launched by the Indian Army on 13 April 1984 to gain control of the freezing heights of the Siachen Glacier?
questions.explanation: Operation Meghdoot was launched on 13 April 1984 under Lt. Gen. P.N. Hoon, preempting Pakistan and establishing Indian military control over the entire Siachen Glacier.

questions.question: Which historic civil liberties petition filed in the Delhi High Court during the Emergency by veteran journalist Kuldip Nayar resulted in an order upholding habeas corpus before the Supreme Court's ADM Jabalpur ruling?
options: A) Bhanudas v. State of Maharashtra
B) Shivkant Shukla v. ADM Jabalpur
C) Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (Delhi High Court, September 1975)
D) Raj Narain v. State of Uttar Pradesh
questions.explanation: The Delhi High Court, led by Justices S. Rangarajan and R.N. Aggarwal, courageously struck down Kuldip Nayar's preventive detention in September 1975, ruling that detention without grounds was invalid.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which secessionist war in the northern Caucasus began in December 1994 when Russian President Boris Yeltsin ordered troops into the rebel republic to restore constitutional order?
questions.explanation: The First Chechen War (1994-1996) ended in military stalemate and the Khasavyurt Accords, granting de facto autonomy to Chechnya until the Second War in 1999.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which bilateral protocol signed between India and China in 2005 recognized the 'political parameters and guiding principles' for resolving the boundary dispute?
options: B) Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for the Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question (April 2005)
C) The Border Peace and Tranquility Agreement of 1993
D) The Sikkim Consular Protocol of 2003
questions.explanation: Signed during Premier Wen Jiabao's visit to New Delhi in April 2005, this agreement established that settled populations in border areas should not be disturbed in any territorial settlement.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the constitutional voting procedure in the International Court of Justice when judges are divided equally (7 against 7)?
options: A) The dispute is immediately referred to the UN Security Council for final judgment
B) The case is automatically dismissed and declared non-justiciable
C) The UN Secretary-General casts the tie-breaking judicial vote
D) The President of the ICJ has a casting vote under Article 55(2) of the ICJ Statute
questions.explanation: Under Article 55 of the ICJ Statute, all questions are decided by a majority of judges present; in the event of an equality of votes, the President (or acting judge) exercises a casting vote.
